panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel shows gross autopsy findings of calcified and serpiginous coronary arteries, a defining feature of GACI, using clinical photo modality (gross). B: Panel B provides a close-up detail of the right coronary artery exhibiting calcification and serpigination, characteristic of GACI. C: The left heart ventricle displays marked hypertrophy, a known consequence of chronic pressure load due to underlying systemic arterial disease (GACI). D: Postnatal cardiac ultrasound of the aorta and pulmonary artery is presented, consistent with the systemic presentation of GACI.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D1, D2). A: Panel A shows extensive calcification of a coronary vessel using H&E staining, a direct manifestation of GACI. B: Panel B shows fibrocalcification and extravascular calcifications within the cardiac left ventricle, consistent with GACI pathology. C: Panel C demonstrates myocardial ischemic degeneration in the left cardiac ventricle, a pathological manifestation linked to the GACI case description. D1: Panel D1 shows cerebral infarction in the brain white matter, which is a pathological finding reported in the context of GACI. D2: Panel D2 shows macrophagic infiltration using CD68 IHC in the area of ischemic necrosis, further documenting the pathological process associated with GACI.

(C) Left cardiac ventricle; the purple areas indicate myocardial ischemic degeneration (H&E; 10.3×). (D1) Brain white matter: infarction in intermediate stage of development (upper left area) (H&E; 2.18×). in_text_mentions: Multinucleated giant cells were not observed where dystrophic calcifications were detected. Marked biventricular myocardial hypertrophy was identified, also involving the septum associated with multiple small foci of myocardial infarction in different stages of development. The foci of infarction were irregularly distributed and localized both in the subepicardial and subendocardial regions. Multiple cerebral infarctions in different stages of development were found (Figure 5).

in_text_mentions: The 2,850 g preterm baby presented cyanotic skin and generalized edema, with hydrothorax, non-infective ascites, and hydrocele. The heart and the large vessels were macroscopically unremarkable. Protein dystrophy was seen in the myocardial fibers (Figure 1), without signs of myocardial ischemia or histological modifications of the coronary arteries.

The intima of large and medium-sized arteries showed marked thickness with degenerative calcifications of lamina elastica interna (Figure 1). In the intima, a proliferation of myofibroblasts that expressed Smooth Muscle Actin (SMA) and Cluster of Differentiation 34 (CD34) was predominant, without proliferation of Cluster of Differentiation 31 (CD31) -marked endothelial cells (Figure 2). Myointimal calcifications at the level of the hepatic vessels associated with necrosis of the perivascular hepatocytes (Figure 1).

At the base of the tongue and in the lower third of the pharynx, hemorrhagic areas of 7–12 mm were seen. Microscopically, the calcification of the intimal layer of the arteries was identified as similar to that of the pulmonary vessels (Figure 1).

A: Panel A displays H&E of periaortic retroperitoneal vessels, showing the systemic involvement of small arteries with dystrophic calcification, which is the hallmark of generalized arterial calcification of infancy. B: Panel B shows H&E of a retroperitoneal artery, demonstrating systemic arterial involvement consistent with Generalized Arterial Calcification of Infancy. C: Panel C displays H&E of a periadrenal artery, confirming the involvement of smaller visceral vessels as seen in GACI. D: Panel D shows H&E of intramuscular arteries of the ilio-psoas muscle, illustrating the wide range of systemic arterial involvement characteristic of the disease.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel A displays the gross specimen of the aorta exhibiting a characteristic grayish-yellow plaque, consistent with generalized arterial calcification of infancy. B: Panel B is a histology slide showing calcification foci specifically beneath the endocardium of the left and right ventricles of the heart. C: Panel C shows patchy calcification distributed beneath the aortic intima and within the general vessel walls, confirming systemic arterial involvement. D: Panel D shows microvascular calcification, specifically in the intimal layer of the carotid artery, consistent with GACI. E: Panel E shows microvascular calcification involving arterial walls, consistent with the systemic involvement of GACI. F: Panel F provides further histological evidence of calcification, documenting the widespread nature of the condition in the patient.

in_text_mentions: An autopsy was conducted after the operation. The HE staining results of the tissue sections revealed significant calcification foci beneath the endocardium of both the left and right ventricles, beneath the aortic intima and within the vascular wall, beneath the intima of the laryngeal arteries, and beneath the intima of arteries within the bladder wall (Figure 4). The final fetal autopsy results confirmed the diagnosis of GACI.

We suspected calcification of the blood vessels and performed CT at 17 days of age, which revealed calcification of the arterial walls in her whole body (Figure 2). No extravascular calcification was noted, and medullary nephrocalcinosis was not seen. We diagnosed the patient with GACI due to severe arterial calcification.
